name: Anthropic
line: Elvis Presley's rights holders sue over 274 songs, asking $150,000 a track.
why: That's about $41 million at the top of the scale, but the bigger bill is the precedent: every catalogue owner now has a price list for training data.

name: OpenAI and Sam Altman
line: Texas sues both, seeking an injunction to keep minors off ChatGPT.
why: If one state wins an age gate, every state can ask for one. Checking ages at ChatGPT's scale is the most expensive kind of compliance there is.

name: Character.AI
line: 31 states and DC object to the rules for selling it out of bankruptcy.
why: Whoever buys it now inherits 32 attorneys general and their child-safety demands, and that is priced into every bid. Hearing Oct 30.

name: Tesla
line: A car on Full Self-Driving killed a 71-year-old on I-80, police say; the second FSD crash in the area this month.
why: Tesla's valuation leans on autonomy. Each fatal crash on the system shifts who sets the pace, from engineers to regulators.

name: Panasonic
line: A staffer put HR data on 334,000 people into a banned AI tool.
why: This year's costliest leaks aren't hacks; they're employees with a paste box. A ban without an approved tool next to it doesn't hold.

name: LiteLLM
line: A master key sat in a public repo since May; an attacker used it to ship a poisoned release that stole AI keys.
why: Thousands of products route their AI calls through tools like this. One leaked credential upstream becomes everyone's breach downstream.

name: Samsung and SK hynix
line: Heading for a combined $139 billion in one quarter's profit, on AI memory demand.
why: Sell shovels in a gold rush: the memory makers are booking the AI profits most of the companies buying AI can't find yet.

name: Moonshot AI
line: Its Kimi K3.1 Pro jumps to fourth on an independent intelligence ranking, three points behind Claude Opus 5.5; open weights due.
why: When near-frontier weights are free to download, paid labs lose pricing power, and nobody can recall a model once it's out.

name: Kazakhstan
line: Joins both the US-led AI bloc and China's, with up to $10 billion of Nvidia data centres on one side and record Chinese investment on the other.
why: Middle powers are learning the AI race pays whoever won't pick a side, until Washington makes them choose, as it now says they must.

name: Axiom Math
line: Says its AI agents produced a computer-checked version of a 15,000-page proof in 24 days; no outside group has rebuilt it yet.
why: A machine-checked proof is something a buyer can verify without trusting the seller, which is exactly what AI-written code lacks. If outsiders reproduce it, chipmakers and banks get a reason to pay for proofs of their software, not just tests.

name: Anthropic
line: Gave US federal, state, local and tribal governments 40% off many of its services and says about 500 government organizations already use Claude.
why: Government seats are sticky: once a state's workflows run on one model, switching costs land on taxpayers, not the vendor. Locking them in while senators question its safety disclosures makes Anthropic harder to regulate against.
